name: Collar
summary: Own 100 shares, buy a protective put and sell a covered call to pay for it - defined floor, defined ceiling, near-zero net cost.

legs.strike_rule: 0.20-0.30 delta OTM, chosen so the credit >= 80% of the put's cost (the ceiling)

max_profit: (call strike - share basis - net debit) x 100
max_loss: (share basis - put strike + net debit) x 100
breakevens: share basis + net debit per share (or minus net credit)

greeks.theta: near zero by design (the short call's decay funds the put's)

when_to_use: Holding a large concentrated share position through uncertainty; locking in gains after a big run; or as the default risk-controlled way to hold ETF shares in an automated fleet. Best when call skew is rich relative to put skew.
entry_rules: Require 100 shares per collar; the call MUST be covered by the shares (level 3 requirement).
Put strike by delta in [0.25, 0.35] or by a max drawdown target: put_strike >= basis x (1 - max_dd_pct).
Call strike chosen as the lowest strike whose credit >= 0.80 x put cost, subject to call_strike >= basis x 1.03 and call_strike >= basis (never cap below cost).
Require (call strike - put strike) >= 8% of spot so the profit band is worth having.
Both legs same expiry; OI >= 250 each; no earnings inside unless the collar is specifically the earnings hedge.
Reject if the net debit exceeds 0.5% of share notional.
management_rules: Manage as a unit; there is no 50% profit rule - the collar is a holding structure, not an income trade.
Roll both legs together at 21-30 DTE to the next cycle, re-striking the put at 0.30 delta and the call at whatever funds it.
If the stock rallies to the call strike, roll the collar UP (higher put and call) for approximately zero cost rather than allowing assignment.
If the stock falls to the put strike, the floor is working; decide whether to monetize the put (sell it, keep the shares and the call) or exit the whole unit.
Never roll the call down below the share basis to fund a higher put.
exit_rules: HARD: the short call is assignable. Flatten it by 15:30 ET on expiration day if ITM or within 0.5% of its strike; close immediately whenever its extrinsic < 0.05 and delta > 0.85.
Ex-dividend guard on the short call: close or roll the day before ex-date if ITM and extrinsic < 1.10 x dividend.
Close the long put before expiry if ITM - auto-exercise would sell the shares at the strike.
Unwind all three legs as one combo order when exiting the position entirely.
assignment_risk: Only the short call is assignable, and it is fully covered by the shares, so the financial risk is bounded - but assignment removes the shares while the long put remains, leaving a naked long put (a bearish position the system did not choose). The reconciliation logic must detect share-count changes and close orphaned puts.
buying_power: Shares plus the net debit; the short call is covered so no additional margin. A collar substantially reduces the maintenance requirement on a margin account.
liquidity_needs: Both wings liquid at 0.25-0.35 delta; OI >= 250 each; combined spread <= 10% of the put's cost.
common_mistakes: Setting the call strike below the share basis and guaranteeing a loss if called; collaring so tightly that the position cannot make money; rolling only one leg and leaving the position lopsided.
zero_dte_notes: A 0DTE collar is a share position with a same-day floor and ceiling - almost all the cost with almost none of the protection. Not worth automating.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
also_filed_under: three-leg-structures (butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, lizards, three-strike ratio spreads, ladders/tree spreads, christmas trees, and three-leg stock+option hybrids)
